f2l.py.summary: Turn a one-item-per-line file into a Python set literal and copy it to the clipboard.
details: Quotes each line (choosing the quote character that does not clash with the content) and writes ``{"a", "b", ...}`` back to the file, then sends the text to ``termux-clipboard-set`` when that command is available.

facal.py.summary: Print a Persian (Jalali) calendar with the current day highlighted.
details: Converts the Gregorian date with its own Jalali arithmetic, prints the month grid with Persian month names, Persian digits and right-to-left alignment (through ``faprint``) and marks today.

faen.py.summary: Browse a Persian↔English dictionary interactively in the terminal.
details: Loads the JSON mapping from ``/sdcard/dic/dic.json`` into both directions, then offers a prompt with lookup, ``:list``, ``:stats``, ``:export`` (CSV), ``:random`` and fuzzy suggestions for near misses. New or edited entries are written back to the same JSON file.

faprinter.py.summary: Print a file line by line with correct right-to-left rendering.
details: Each line is passed through ``faprint`` (the Persian text shaper) and printed, so mixed Persian/English text keeps its visual order in a terminal.

fasort.py.summary: Sort a Persian word-list file in Persian alphabetical order.
details: Reads the lines of the file, sorts them with a Persian collation key (letter order and diacritic handling) and writes the sorted list back to the same file.

feloai.py.summary: Ask the felo superagent for a script and save the reply as a dated log file.
details: Runs ``felo-sa.mjs`` with the arguments given on the command line, writes a header with the prompt and a footer with the elapsed time around the returned text and stores everything under ``~/tmp/apps`` as a timestamped Markdown file.
example: $ feloai 'write a python script that renames files'

feloer.py.summary: Write module docstrings for Python files with the felo superagent.
details: Sends a simplified view of each module to ``felo-sa.mjs``, cleans the answer into a Google-style docstring and inserts it (with ``--force`` even over an existing one). Options cover the glob to walk, concurrency, delay between calls, a log file and a dry run; files that already fail noisily are skipped.

filetools.py.summary: Query and move files by age, size and extension with one subcommand CLI.
details: ``scan-ctime`` reports files created in the last N minutes, ``filter``/``filter-recursive`` list files by extension, size and age, ``recent-modified`` and ``same-day`` select by mtime, ``move`` relocates matches into a destination directory, and ``newest``/``oldest``/``btime`` show the extremes (birth time is read through ``statx`` where available).

find_big_files.py.summary: List the files below the current directory that exceed a size threshold.
details: Prints every regular (non-symlink) file larger than the threshold, one megabyte by default, as a path relative to the current directory with a human-readable size.

find_dup_folders.py.summary: Find folders with identical contents by hashing their files.
details: Hashes the relative name and content of every file in each folder below the current directory (skipping nested duplicates) and prints the groups of folders whose hash matches.

find_empty_wheels.py.summary: Move wheels that contain no code into an ``empty_wheels`` folder.
details: A ``.whl`` is empty when it has no ``.py``/``.pyi``/``.so`` member; those files are reported and moved into ``./empty_wheels``, invalid archives are skipped with a warning.

find_req.py.summary: Find the installed distributions that depend on a given package.
details: Scans the ``METADATA`` files of the user ``site-packages`` for a ``Requires-Dist:`` line mentioning the package name and prints the distribution directory names that match.
find_req.py.notes: The scan root is the module constant ``cwd``; adjust it for other Python versions.

find_scripts.py.summary: Count the executable scripts below the current directory by interpreter.
details: Reads the shebang of every extension-less file (skipping binaries and virtual-env/cache directories), resolves ``env`` lookups and tallies how many scripts use each known interpreter; ``--verbose`` also prints the paths.

finglish.py.summary: Rename Persian file names below the current directory to Finglish (Latin script).
details: Maps the Persian letters to their usual Latin transliterations, normalises the result with Unicode NFKD and renames the files that contain non-ASCII characters.
